name: Linda Williams
chief_complaint: Feeling unwell after taking multiple paracetamol tablets
opening_statement: I'm really worried... I took way too many paracetamol tablets last night after an argument with my boyfriend. I felt really upset and just wanted the emotional pain to stop. Now I feel sick and my friends made me come to hospital.
emotional_baseline: Anxious and tearful, displaying signs of emotional distress. Cooperative but appears frightened about potential consequences. Demonstrates insight into severity of situation.

rag_citations.reference: Toxicology - Paracetamol poisoning: Early symptoms (0-24 hours) include nausea, vomiting, pallor, and malaise
Paracetamol overdose: Abdominal pain may develop within 24 hours, particularly right upper quadrant tenderness indicating early hepatotoxicity
Acute paracetamol toxicity stage 1 (0-24 hours): Patients present with non-specific symptoms including malaise, pallor, diaphoresis

past_medical_history.complications: previous self-harm episode (superficial cuts) 6 months ago

allergies: No known drug allergies. No food allergies.
family_history: Mother has history of depression, treated with antidepressants. Father has hypertension. Maternal grandmother died from breast cancer age 62. No family history of liver disease or substance abuse.

social_history.occupation: University student (first year Bachelor of Arts)
social_history.alcohol: Social drinker, approximately 4-6 standard drinks per week on weekends
social_history.recreational_drugs: Denies current use, admits to trying cannabis once at age 17
social_history.diet: Irregular eating patterns, relies on convenience foods
social_history.relationships: Recently broke up with boyfriend of 8 months, describes relationship as 'on and off' and emotionally turbulent
social_history.support_network: Close relationship with mother and 2 university friends who brought her to hospital
social_history.stressors: University assessments due, relationship breakdown, financial pressures from student loans

examination_findings.general_appearance: Young female, appears stated age, tearful and anxious, alert and oriented to time, place and person. Appears pale and diaphoretic.
examination_findings.cardiovascular: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. Peripheral pulses palpable and equal. No peripheral edema. Capillary refill <2 seconds.
examination_findings.respiratory: Chest clear to auscultation bilaterally. No respiratory distress. Equal air entry.
examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, mild epigastric and right upper quadrant tenderness on palpation. No guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds present and normal. No organomegaly palpated. Murphy's sign negative.
examination_findings.neurological: Alert and oriented x3. Cranial nerves II-XII intact. Normal tone and power in all limbs. Reflexes 2+ and symmetrical. No asterixis. No focal neurological deficits.
examination_findings.psychiatric: Tearful and anxious. Demonstrates remorse and concern. Denies current suicidal ideation but admits impulsive act during emotional crisis. Willing to engage with mental health services. Insight appears appropriate.

bedside.result: Sinus rhythm, rate 98 bpm, normal intervals and axis, no ST changes

pathology.interpretation: Significantly elevated, above treatment line on nomogram

expected_management.action: Commence N-acetylcysteine (NAC) infusion immediately - 150mg/kg IV over 60 minutes, then 50mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100mg/kg over 16 hours
expected_management.rationale: Patient presents within 24 hours with paracetamol level above treatment line on nomogram. NAC is hepatoprotective and prevents hepatotoxicity if given within 8-10 hours
expected_management.pbs_restriction: NAC is PBS listed for paracetamol poisoning without restriction

expected_management.action: 4-hourly vital signs, monitor for anaphylactoid reactions to NAC (rash, bronchospasm), repeat LFTs and INR at 12-24 hours
expected_management.rationale: NAC can cause anaphylactoid reactions in 5-15% of patients. Need to monitor for hepatotoxicity progression

expected_management.action: Mental health crisis team review, suicide risk assessment, consider Mental Health Act assessment if required
expected_management.rationale: Deliberate self-poisoning requires psychiatric assessment. Patient has background of depression and previous self-harm

expected_management.action: IV fluids for hydration, antiemetics (ondansetron 4mg IV PRN for nausea), maintain nil by mouth until NAC infusion established
expected_management.rationale: Supportive management of symptoms, ensure adequate hydration for NAC infusion

expected_management.action: One-to-one nursing observation, remove sharps and ligature risks from environment, involve family/support persons with patient consent
expected_management.rationale: Patient safety in context of deliberate self-harm and ongoing suicide risk

expected_management.action: Complete 21-hour NAC protocol, repeat paracetamol level and LFTs, psychiatric clearance before discharge, safety plan and crisis contacts, GP follow-up within 48 hours, ongoing mental health support
expected_management.rationale: Ensure complete treatment of poisoning and appropriate mental health discharge planning

critical_errors.error: Failing to commence N-acetylcysteine within 8 hours of ingestion
critical_errors.consequence: Massive increase in risk of fulminant hepatic failure and potential death. NAC is most effective within 8-10 hours of paracetamol ingestion.
High risk of repeat self-harm or completed suicide. Deliberate self-poisoning requires mandatory mental health review.

critical_errors.error: Not interpreting paracetamol level on treatment nomogram correctly
critical_errors.consequence: Patient level is significantly above treatment line - failure to recognize this delays life-saving treatment

critical_errors.error: Failing to monitor for anaphylactoid reactions during NAC infusion
critical_errors.consequence: NAC reactions can be severe (bronchospasm, hypotension) and require immediate management. Failure to monitor endangers patient.

critical_errors.error: Not checking for co-ingestions (alcohol, other medications, recreational drugs)
critical_errors.consequence: Poly-pharmacy overdose may require different management. Alcohol increases paracetamol hepatotoxicity risk.

critical_errors.error: Inadequate safety planning or one-to-one observation in ED
critical_errors.consequence: Patient at risk of absconding or further self-harm while in ED. Best practice is close observation for deliberate overdose.

fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent case for AMC clinical examination. Paracetamol overdose is high-yield emergency topic with time-critical management. Case appropriately calibrated as Medium difficulty - 3 comorbidities (depression, anxiety, previous self-harm) create complexity without being overwhelming. NAC protocol knowledge is essential, as is psychiatric assessment requirement. Realistic presentation timeframe (overnight ingestion, presents morning) and clinical findings consistent with stage 1 paracetamol toxicity. Critical errors appropriately severe - failing NAC or psych assessment are genuine auto-fails in real practice. Learning objectives cover toxicology, mental health, and medico-legal aspects comprehensively.
fracp_reviews.suggestions: None - case meets all AMC examination standards for Emergency specialty station.

fracp_reviews.comments: Mental health aspects of this case are accurately portrayed and clinically appropriate. Patient demonstrates typical presentation of impulsive self-harm in context of relationship breakdown and pre-existing depression. Risk assessment elements are realistic - previous self-harm, ongoing stressors, but current remorse and engagement suggest moderate rather than high ongoing risk. Appropriate to include Mental Health Act consideration without being prescriptive about outcome. Social history details (student stress, relationship issues, support network) provide important context for holistic assessment. Critical error regarding psychiatric clearance is absolutely correct - no patient with deliberate self-poisoning should be discharged without mental health review.
fracp_reviews.suggestions: Case appropriately balances medical emergency with psychiatric complexity. Well-suited for AMC examination.

learning_objectives.objective: Recognize clinical presentation and timeframes of paracetamol poisoning stages (0-24hr asymptomatic/mild GI, 24-72hr hepatotoxicity, 72-96hr peak hepatic injury)
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Medical Expert - Toxicology and poisoning management

learning_objectives.objective: Correctly interpret paracetamol levels using treatment nomogram and understand critical 8-hour window for NAC efficacy
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Medical Expert - Interpretation of investigations and time-critical decision making

learning_objectives.objective: Demonstrate knowledge of N-acetylcysteine dosing protocol (150mg/kg, 50mg/kg, 100mg/kg) and monitoring for anaphylactoid reactions
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Medical Expert - Pharmacotherapy in emergency toxicology

learning_objectives.objective: Perform appropriate suicide risk assessment in context of deliberate self-poisoning, including previous attempts, current ideation, and protective factors
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Communicator & Collaborator - Sensitive discussion of mental health and self-harm

learning_objectives.objective: Understand mandatory psychiatric review requirements for deliberate overdose and appropriate use of Mental Health Act if required
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Professional & Scholar - Medico-legal obligations in mental health presentations

learning_objectives.objective: Integrate medical emergency management with holistic assessment of psychosocial factors (relationship stress, university pressures, support networks)
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Health Advocate - Addressing social determinants of health in young adults

learning_objectives.objective: Develop safety plan including environmental risk reduction, family involvement, crisis contacts, and GP/mental health follow-up within 48 hours
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Collaborator - Multidisciplinary discharge planning for complex psychosocial cases

learning_objectives.objective: Recognize need to screen for co-ingestions (alcohol, other medications, recreational drugs) and understand alcohol as hepatotoxicity risk factor in paracetamol overdose
learning_objectives.amc_alignment: Medical Expert - Comprehensive assessment in toxicology cases
